summary: You present a coherent Australian reef-monitoring concept and address most required mission topics, supported by STK outputs. To reach the next rubric level, strengthen the evidence for feasibility: specify the operator and operational responsibilities, quantify imaging and communications performance, resolve orbital and end-of-life inconsistencies, and improve the sources and presentation of your evidence.

criteria.C1: In your Introduction, you explain the reef-monitoring need, justify using one spacecraft, and identify likely customers such as CSIRO and BOM. To reach Accomplished, explicitly name the spacecraft operator and clarify its responsibilities, and support the rationale with complete, appropriate references.
criteria.C2: Your Launch, Orbit, Ground Control & Communications, and Mission Duration & EOL sections cover the main design topics, and STK access results provide useful evidence. To reach Accomplished, demonstrate feasibility with imaging-performance and communications/link-budget calculations, specify orbital epoch and local solar time, establish launch and ground-station compatibility, and develop a consistent, quantified disposal plan.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion brings together the principal mission choices and notes uncertainty about the proposed launch vehicle. To reach Accomplished, use the evidence in the report to assess whether the design can meet reef-monitoring needs, identify unresolved limitations, and state how they affect mission feasibility.
criteria.C4: Your report has an Executive Summary, clear section headings, and relevant visuals and tables. To reach Accomplished, use consistent numbering and captions for figures and tables, correct language errors, and provide complete, consistently cited references; replace the Wikipedia citation with an appropriate source.

next_steps: In Orbit, specify the epoch and local time of the ascending or descending node, then support the 600 km choice with resolution, swath, and reef-coverage analysis; clarify what the orbital elements establish about illumination.

In Ground Control & Communications, verify Mount Pleasant’s TT&C compatibility and operational access, add a link budget and data-rate analysis, and check the access table for the duplicated entry. In Mission Duration & EOL, size and assess the drag sail and explain disposal consistently with the no-thruster design.

In the Introduction, name the operator and its responsibilities. In the Conclusion, evaluate mission performance against the evidence and remaining uncertainties; throughout, improve figure/table captions and replace bare URLs and the Wikipedia citation with complete, suitable references.
